newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS - ZVEREVA-FERNANDEZ RALLY TO WIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS - ZVEREVA-FERNANDEZ RALLY TO WIN.

text.p: American Gigi Fernandez and Natasha Zvereva of Belarus, the second seeded team, beat top seeds Jana Novotna of the Czech Republic and Arantxa Sanchez Vicario of Spain 1-6 6-1 6-4 on Sunday to retain the U.S. Open women's doubles title.
It was the 12th Grand Slam title for Fernandez and Zvereva over a four-year span and their third U.S. crown, but they would not commit themselves to defending the championship again in l997.
"I haven't made up my mind yet," Zvereva said.
Together since l992, they won three Wimbledons, four French and two Australian titles in addition to their trio of U.S. Opens.
"We got together, I guess, when our old partners dumped us," Zvereva said. Zvereva had teamed with Larisa Neiland, Fernandez with Novotna.
"This was only our fifth tournament this year," Fernandez said. "Natasha got injured after Australia and then I got hurt. We didn't have fun this year."
This year, Fernandez-Zvereva combined for a 19-4 record, but only one title, the Pan Pacific in Tokyo, before Sunday's win.
"We got our butt kicked in the first set," Zvereva said. "I was ready but they came out so fast and the level of tennis was so high."
Fernandez-Zvereva quickly recovered and won the third-set duel by breaking Sanchez' service at love in the ninth game. Zvereva held service at 30 in the final game.
Fernandez and Zvereva shared $240,000 first prize. Novotna and Sanchez, the U.S. Open winners two years ago, received $120,000.
